articles.title: Dungeons And Dragons Icons Could Take The TTRPG To A Modern-Day Setting
articles.summary: The D&D Icons initiative, led by actor and longtime D&D fanatic Joe Manganiello, brings today's Dungeons & Dragons game together with famous series creators of the past, like author R.A. Salvatore's The Legend of Drizzt.
body: Speaking to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell at Gen Con 2026, Manganiello stressed that modern-day settings could be part of the Icons program, too.

"There [are] also lots of other things that I want for Icons in the future," he said. "I think that there's a great present-day game that pushes genetics and military. We're moving at such a rapid pace, but I think there could be a game that takes place in our modern world. There are also some other worlds of D&D that I think could be revisited in new and exciting ways that weren't maximized their first time around."

Manganiello, whose official title is chief creative officer, is keeping specifics secret for now, but it sounds like, for fans of more modern fantasy adventures, D&D Icons could be for you. Could something futuristic like Halo or Horizon: Zero Dawn make sense for the D&D ruleset? Only time will tell, but it could open up the D&D experience to an even wider audience. Wizards has experimented with more modern content in the past, so it's not unprecedented.

articles.title: Until Dawn 2 Was Co-Developed by Dispatch Developer AdHoc Studio
articles.summary: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptach, helped develop Until Dawn 2. In a new PlayStation Blog post, Until Dawn 2 developer Firesprite confirmed that AdHoc helped craft the story of the new horror game.
body: "We’ve partnered with our friends at AdHoc Studio – the brilliant minds behind the acclaimed Dispatch – so you can expect a deeply layered story packed with rich characters, razor-sharp dialogue, fraught relationships, tough decisions, and yes… more than a few gruesome deaths," reads the post. "Every choice, every interaction can ripple with dramatic consequences."

AdHoc has been around for nearly a decade, but only released its first game last year. The team is largely comprised of ex-Telltale, Ubisoft, and Night School Studio talent, which has allowed them to use their narrative expertise for new titles like Dispatch. The 2025 superhero game was a refreshing experience take on a tried and true genre with nuanced relationships, hilarious and compelling writing, and meaningful choices.

Given AdHoc only rose to prominence last year, it's unclear when they were brought on to Until Dawn 2. They could've been a late addition to punch up the game following the success of Dispatch, or Firesprite could've recognized their potential early on and brought them in a couple of years ago. Either way, it's great to see the AdHoc team being utilized on a franchise that means so much to horror fans.
points: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptach, helped develop Until Dawn 2.

articles.title: STALZONE Is an Extraction Shooter with MMO DNA
articles.summary: Back in June, developer EXBO rebranded free-to-play open-world PvPvE extraction shooter STALCRAFT: X as STALZONE alongside a graphical upgrade, reworking of its starting missions and locations, PvP rebalancing, and other big changes.
body: While STALZONE is an extraction shooter, it doesn’t play like most other games in the genre. You don’t simply drop into one self-contained map for a session. It’s a persistent world where factions fight over territory and the balance of power can shift while you’re offline. And there are NPCs, quests, and dungeons like you’d find in an MMORPG.

It takes place in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, which has been twisted by anomalies and overrun by mutants. You’ll use a detector to safely navigate the anomalies, and there are hidden caches and artifacts to find, constantly shifting weather, and global cataclysms like an energy emission that turns the sky red and can kill all living things.

The 50-hour story is told across two main campaigns, and the latest update added English voice acting. This is not an extraction shooter where you need to sift through item descriptions to decipher the world’s lore, it’s all laid out through the main story and the many side quests.

articles.title: The New Gundam Game Has A Collector’s Edition Just For Gunpla Sickos Like Me
articles.summary: Gundam Rogue Orbit is a break from tradition for Bandai Namco, as new entries in the franchise typically debut as an anime series first, then as a line of collectible model kits.
body: Like other special editions from Bandai Namco, Gundam Rogue Orbit combines a physical copy of the game with a few physical in-game goodies. It's the inclusion of a High-Grade model kit based on the new Gundam Helix mobile suit that could make this collector's edition sought after, as it will be exclusive to the game. Gundam model kits aren't usually hard to come by as Bandai Namco regularly keeps store shelves restocked with them, but the HG Helix model looks like a rare exception to that rule.

If you are planning to grab one, it's worth noting that HG Gundam model kits are 1/144-scale figures and are designed to appeal to casual builders with their moderate detail, minimal foil stickers, and durable design. You won't need too many tools to build one either, and the Helix design features a lot of panels and other mechanical details, so that could be a nice kit to build. The new trailer for the game also teased other shells that you can apply to the Helix to shake up its look, including an RX-78-2 skin and a red Zaku-inspired look that would make Char Aznable proud.

articles.summary: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann says that neither he nor the studio are involved with the third season of the HBO TV adaptation of the beloved video game, but says that the developer "isn't done" with the franchise yet.
body: Naughty Dog is currently focused on its next game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, which was a no-show at today's Sony State of Play, but did recently wrap cinematic shooting. It does not yet have a release window.

On The Last of Us TV show, meanwhile, Peter Sarsgaard has been cast in a role for an original character not featured in the games, while Li Jun Li was cast as Miriam, among numerous other cast announcements. We also recently learned that Matthew McConaughey turned down the part of Joel, which of course went to Pedro Pascal.

articles.title: Game Pass Is Getting Worse, And More Expensive
articles.summary: Microsoft has made a big announcement about one of the big perks of Xbox Game Pass, cloud streaming, and the news is not great. Starting in November, Microsoft will put limits on how many hours per month people can use the service, and then allow people to pay more to unlock more time.
body: For people who want or need more monthly streaming hours, Microsoft will allow people to buy more--but pricing was not announced.

"We’re introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer. Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost," Microsoft said. The company added that it will "listen closely" to player feedback and make adjustments if necessary.

Xbox's cloud gaming service runs on Azure servers, and the Azure business is booming. For the first time ever, Microsoft just revealed how much money it makes on Azure quarterly, and the latest numbers showed $29.4 billion in sales. As relayed by Reuters, that's behind Amazon's latest quarterly revenue for AWS of $42.2 billion but ahead of Google's $24.8 billion cloud business results.

articles.title: A Long-Dormant Blizzard Franchise Could Be Coming To Dungeons And Dragons
articles.summary: Dungeons & Dragons is no stranger to crossovers with other IP, and a collaboration with Blizzard's World of Warcraft also already on the way. However, that may not be the only Blizzard crossover we get in D&D, as both Wizards of the Coast and Blizzard teased recently.
body: Speaking to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell during Gen Con 2026, head of Dungeons & Dragons Dan Ayoub made it clear that he would love a StarCraft crossover.

"I will say this, since I am sitting here with [World of Warcraft VP] Holly Longdale, who is super persuasive and has cool stuff: I think StarCraft would be badass," Ayoub said. "As I said earlier today, I quite literally almost flunked out of university because of StarCraft. That one gives me the feels."
The two exchanged conspiratorial smiles before Longdale replied, “Hmmm. I think we should talk. I know a guy." Ayoub laughed, then added, "I think I know where to find you."

Blizzard was not giving any more details on a potential StarCraft crossover and at this point, it’s not clear if it’s even officially in the works. However, their coy nature discussing it has us very intrigued.

articles.title: 'God of War' Star Dave Bautista Shows Off Progress In Getting Kratos-Sized
articles.summary: Playing the God of War in the upcoming Prime Video television series comes with certain expectations. Kratos, the series' protagonist, is a demigod with chiseled abs most people could only dream of.
body: Bautista is working on it, though, as evidenced by a recent short clip the actor shared on social media. The Guardians of the Galaxy star said he was three weeks into his new weight training program, and that he had "2 more months to get where I need to be." Where Bautista needs to be is Kratos-sized and sculpted.

Bautista makes it sound like filming for Kratos hasn't begun yet, which makes sense. The production restarted in summer 2026 after an on-set accident. The original actor who was cast as Kratos, Ryan Hurst, tore his bicep while performing a stunt. Prime Video had to scrap several episodes that were reportedly already completed.

Hurst's initial casting was also the source of much controversy, as fans believed that the show did a poor job of capturing Kratos' menacing look. Early photographs hailing from the set were ridiculed on social media after they were released. Fans received Bautista's casting with more enthusiasm, but the actor still faces the daunting task of bulking up to borderline unrealistic proportions.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation finally gets a 2027 release date, as Final Fantasy Resonance gets a surprise demo
articles.summary: We already knew that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation was going to launch sometime in 'spring 2027 ', but today director Naoki Hamaguchi took to Sony's State of Play livestream to inform us all that the game has a locked-in release date: 8th April, 2027.
body: In case you're unaware, the game is the final part of a trilogy that began with Final Fantasy 7 Remake and tells the story of the original FF7 in three parts. This closing chapter sees Cloud finally catch up to Sephiroth as the heroic gang tries to prevent the almighty meteor from colliding with the planet. To make matters worse, the existential threat to all life on the continent has also awoken planetary defense mechanisms known as Weapons which, in defending the planet at all costs, may also pose a risk to humanity. D'oh.

The State of Play trailer showed off new gameplay footage, showing us how Cid's airship - the Highwind - can be used to travel to the regions of the world. This will be the biggest game in the trilogy, by far, including all the locations we've seen in the other games, plus some new original areas, too. It's very much 'the final disc' of the original FF7, if you ask me, and has been scaled appropriately. I recently had a big chat with Hamaguchi, and was taken aback by his humbleness and vision for the trilogy. If you're excited about what the game has to offer, I encourage you to give the feature a read.

articles.title: Supergirl Lands Official Streaming Date on HBO Max
articles.summary: DC Studios and Warner Bros. released Supergirl earlier this year in theaters as the second film in James Gunn's nascent cinematic DC Universe. Despite a solid star in the lead role and a story adapted from one of the character's most well-received comics, the movie failed to garner widespread…
body: Now Warner Bros. and DC Studios have confirmed that Supergirl will land on HBO Max next week.

Supergirl follows Milly Alcock as the titular hero, also known as Kara Zor-El, as she becomes embroiled in a hunt for the villainous Krem of the Yellow Hill after he poisons Krypto. The hunt also brings Kara into contact with the young girl, Ruthey, who enlists Kara's help in a mission of revenge, revealing that Krem killed her father as well.

The True Grit -inspired story takes the unlikely pair across the galaxy to complete their shared search for revenge. The film was directed by Craig Gillespie and written by Ana Nogueira. The story was based on the Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow comic series written by Tom King, who has been tapped by Gunn to serve as a core architect and writer for the DCU.
DC Studios' Supergirl will officially begin streaming on HBO Max starting on Sept. 10.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Story DLC Starring Two Fan-Favorite Characters Confirmed
articles.summary: Square Enix announced during today's State of Play that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will be released on April 8, 2027, finally delivering a conclusion to the FF7 Remake trilogy after seven years.
body: Revelation 's release, however, will not be the actual end of the remake trilogy. The developer has also revealed that the third entry in the series will receive two pieces of story DLC focused on fan-favorite characters Sephiroth and Vincent Valentine.

So far the remake trilogy has received only one major story DLC in the form of Remake 's Episode INTERmission. The Yuffie-focused chapter released almost a year after Remake and told an original story about what the young ninja was up to in Midgar during the events of the first game before she met up with Cloud and the rest of the gang. While both Sephiroth and Vincent are characters with extensive backstories that have been expanded upon in the extended Final Fantasy 7 lore, it is likely their respective story DLCs won't retread old ground.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance is somehow even better than all those beautiful trailers make it look
articles.summary: Let me paint you a picture. It's the second day of Gamescom 2026, everyone is hot and sweaty, the schedule is rapidly deteriorating as previews run late, interviewees go over their allotted times, and dashing from booth to booth adds minutes onto every single journey.
body: No skin off my nose; I'm going to play Resonance on Switch 2 at home anyway. This is the best kind-of preview. Thing is, I'm crammed into a room with eight PS5 units chugging away, 10 sweaty bodies all sitting and standing in close proximity to each other, and my massive backpack slung over my shoulder as I hoist the Switch 2 as close to my face as possible to see what's going on in the middle of all the washed-out overhead lights.

Yet, in the middle of all these adverse conditions, I completely lost myself in the world of Final Fantasy Resonance. It's absolutely spectacular. Even squinting to make out the game, chirping its merry sounds to me through a set of fairly cheap headphones, I could just taste the production values of this unexpectedly lush game. The battle system is deep, rewarding, and hard, the visuals are absolutely gorgeous, and the cameo 'summons' of Final Fantasy characters past and present are so 'hype' that I didn't skip a single animation. I can't wait to get this full game in my hands.

articles.title: Until Dawn 2's sun-kissed horror gets a PS5 release date - and the studio behind last year's brilliant Dispatch is involved
articles.summary: Following its big Summer Game Fest unveiling earlier this year, Until Dawn 2 has been given a release date as part of Sony's latest State of Play showcase. And it's not far away at all, launching for PS5 in the suitably dark depths of winter: arriving 28th January next year.
body: As we learned previously, some big changes are afoot in Until Dawn 2. For starters, the snow-covered alpine resort setting of the first game is making way for sun-kissed tropical climes, where a successful crew of TV ghosthunters (the Dead True) is about to embark on its latest assignment.

"After an investigation at Blackwood Sanitorium takes a chilling turn," Sony explains in its release date announcement, "an encounter with supernatural survivor Yoona leads them to Akishima Island, a remote paradise abandoned for decades and hiding secrets far older than any of them imagined."

New characters does, of course, mean a new cast - but, notably, one familiar face is returning: Peter Stormare, who played Until Dawn 1's memorably unhinged psychiatrist Dr. Hill, is back and will presumably be fulfilling a similar role. Quite how that'll work in story terms, however - given some of the things we learn in the original game - Sony hasn't yet said.

State of Play Japan will showcase upcoming games from game studios in Japan and Asia, including new gameplay, announcements, news and more.
